items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: He said that his agent, a guy named Milt, Milt Something, I can't remember his name...

ctx.x: think the trio wasn't working, or we had just disbanded or something. Anyway, I went up and did this week with him. And while I was there, he was telling me that he owed the agents in New York...I think he owed something like $25,000. He was telling me that he'd gone into debt, and he just couldn't handle the band, he couldn't keep the band any longer. He said he was going to do a single, and he would be happy to have me as his pianist and musical director or whatever. But I think he told me he could only pay me…

Well, $100 a week wasn't good money under any standards, you know. But it was a thing where I could eke out a couple of dollars to send home to my family, and find some cheap place to live. Anyway, I decided I'd go with him. I think another main attraction was that we were going back to 52nd Street, and we were going for an extended engagement there. So I felt like if I went back to New York, while I was there perhaps some other things could happen.
